nodes.label: A woman in her 60s presented with a new pruritic rash

The rash initially developed on the patient's legs 13 days before presentation and subsequently progressed to her feet, arms, hands, and trunk; associated symptoms included a burning sensation and occasional pain.

Physical examination showed numerous erythematous edematous coalescing papules and plaques on the upper and lower extremities and scattered erythematous papules and plaques on the back and buttocks; some plaques were annular and polycyclic in configuration with central hyperpigmentation, while the chest, abdomen, face, and oral mucosa were clear.

Medical history was notable for endometrial adenocarcinoma status post hysterectomy and recent postoperative radiotherapy totaling 50.4 Gy in 28 fractioned doses, completed 4 days after the onset of the rash.
The patient denied any new medications, exposure to chemotherapy, imaging with intravenous contrast, or recent travel; the remainder of her review of systems was unremarkable.
Skin biopsy shows dense perivascular and interstitial infiltrate with innumerable eosinophils, without leukocytoclasia or erythrocyte extravasation.
The rash is a paraneoplastic eosinophilic dermatosis
Tumor staging and radiotherapy details have not been obtained
Infection and hematologic disorders have not been excluded
Paraneoplastic eosinophilic dermatosis associated with endometrial adenocarcinoma
Autoimmune eosinophilic dermatosis (e.g., eosinophilic annular erythema)
Eosinophilic dermatosis secondary to occult hematologic disorder or hypereosinophilic syndrome
Skin biopsy shows no typical radiation-induced changes (e.g., epidermal atrophy, telangiectasia, atypical fibroblasts)
Eosinophilic dermatosis secondary to occult infection
